blocks.content: A Bill shall be deemed to be a Money Bill if it contains only provisions dealing with all or any of the matters specified in Article 110.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha and requires the prior recommendation of the President.
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha decides whether a bill is a Money Bill or not, and their decision is final.
The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a Money Bill; it can only make recommendations within 14 days.
If the Rajya Sabha fails to return the bill within 14 days, it is deemed to have been passed by both Houses in the form passed by the Lok Sabha.
There is no constitutional provision for a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament in the case of a Money Bill.

rows: Either Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha

items: Money Bills cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha or without the prior recommendation of the President.
The endorsement of the Speaker on a Money Bill is final and cannot be questioned in any court of law or in either House of Parliament.
Rajya Sabha's delay capacity for a Money Bill is strictly restricted to 14 days, after which it automatically passes.
Joint sitting under Article 108 is NOT applicable to Money Bills.
